svg.aria-label: Microsoft 365 Copilot architecture: a declarative agent published in your Microsoft tenant signs the user in to a dedicated PlaidCloud OAuth client, then calls the PlaidCloud MCP endpoint where a deny-by-default access level and the user's own permissions gate every tool call. Credential, identity, and access-control tools are never reachable.
svg.text: Microsoft 365 Copilot — What Makes It Different
Copilot cannot be pointed at an arbitrary server, so PlaidCloud ships a published agent package and a pre-registered OAuth client instead.
YOUR MICROSOFT 365 TENANT
A person in Teams, Outlook, or M365 chat
Asks in plain language — no PlaidCloud window, no SQL
"Why did allocated IT cost for Atlanta go up last quarter?"
PlaidCloud declarative agent
A .zip package you download from the control plane and
your Teams admin uploads to the org app catalog.
Named for your workspace; one package per workspace.
Microsoft-brokered sign-in
Copilot opens its own sign-in window and stores the result
against a fixed Microsoft redirect address.
Roughly monthly re-sign-in, not daily.
YOUR PLAIDCLOUD TENANT
PlaidCloud identity — a dedicated Copilot client
A confidential OAuth client per tenant realm, with the Microsoft redirect address
pre-registered and a longer refresh window so sign-in lasts about a month.
The person signs in as themselves — no shared service account.
Access level — deny by default
Resolved on the server from the role an administrator assigned, not from anything
the token claims. No role means no data, and the agent says so plainly.
Read-only · list, describe, read, explain
Read/write · permitted writes · Full · the person's whole toolset
Most permissive role wins. The level is a ceiling, never an expansion.
Curated MCP server
Every call re-checks the level, the person's own scopes and ACLs, and the denylist.
Your project data
Read live under that person's permissions — the answer is a real query result.
Never reachable through Copilot, at any level
Credential and connection settings · identity and group management · access-control changes · publishing · deployable code. These stay human-only.
